layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The microstructure of duplex stainless steels (DSS) consists of two phases, aust-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enite and ferrite. Both phases are present in relatively large separate domains and in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approximately equal volume fractions. Super duplex stainless steels (SDSS) are de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fined as steels for which the pitting resistance equivalent number (PREN = wt.%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exceeds 40 [1–4].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In SDSS the corrosion properties of both ferrite and austenite depend strongly on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the actual chemical composition. The main alloying elements chromium, molyb-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denum, nickel, and nitrogen are not equally distributed in ferrite and austenite: The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenite is enriched in nickel and nitrogen, while the ferrite is enriched in chromium

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and molybdenum. The partitioning of these elements affects the corrosion resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of both, the single phases and the entire alloy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DSS, and in particular SDSS, offer a very favourable combination of mechanical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties, especially high strength, and high corrosion resistance. Newly developed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SDSS exhibit an extraordinary resistance to chloride induced corrosion. These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties open a large field of applications in marine and petrochemical industries.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.1. Element partitioning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It has been suggested that the corrosion resistance of SDSS is determined by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance of the weaker phase [5,6]. Hence, an optimised alloy should have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: equal PREN for both phases, ferrite and austenite. The partitioning behaviour of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromium and molybdenum as well as the volume fraction of ferrite and austenite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have a strong influence on the composition of the individual phases: For example,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Since

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , an increase of chromium and molybdenum leads to a higher

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: PREN of the ferrite, but also to a higher phase volume fraction of the ferrite, i.e.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decreases. The supplementary addition of chromium and molybdenum is restricted,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not only due to the austenite-ferrite volume fraction change, but also due to the fact,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that a high chromium and molybdenum content in the ferrite implies a high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proneness to intermetallic phase formation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Nitrogen is strongly enriched in the austenite [6] and thus improves the corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance by increasing the PREN of the austenite [7]. Moreover, it has been re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ported that nitrogen also reduces the tendency for sigma phase precipitations by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reducing the chromium enrichment in the ferrite [8,9]. Therefore, a high nitrogen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content would allow a further increase of chromium and molybdenum. Apart from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the partitioning of chromium and molybdenum, nitrogen leads to a higher volume

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fraction of austenite. In order to obtain a balanced phase distribution, i.e. equal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volume fractions of ferrite and austenite, the content of the other austenite forming

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: element, nickel, has to be considered parallel to the nitrogen content [6]. The ni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trogen solubility in high nitrogen steels is enhanched by adding manganese [10], but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the low solubility of nitrogen in the ferrite causes precipitation of chromium nitrides.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The quenching temperature has the strongest effect on the element partitioning.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The partitioning is more significant at lower temperatures. This tendency may be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explained on the basis of the thermodynamical concept of entropy and due to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: changing equilibrium of the phase volume fractions of the ferrite and the austenite.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The phase volume fraction of the ferrite decreases with decreasing temperature. A

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: smaller ferrite volume fraction leads to a higher concentration of chromium and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: molybdenum in the ferrite phase, i.e.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increases. On the other hand, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: larger austenite volume fraction leads to a lower concentation of nitrogen and nickel,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decreases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the present Part I, five different alloys with varying PREN of the single phases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been investigated with respect to the general corrosion resistance and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance of the single phases in chloride containing environments. Special

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attention is paid to the comparison between the empirical pitting resistance equiv-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alent number of austenite and ferrite and the experimental measurements. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formation of precipitates such as sigma phase, chromium nitrides and secondary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenite of the Widmannstätten type and their influence on the corrosion resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: will be considered in a second paper (Part II) which is directly connected to this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: present Part I.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.8. Microelectrochemical method – electrochemical microcell

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In order to perform electrochemical experiments within the micrometer range, it is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: necessary to reduce the surface area of the exposed sample. In the applied technique,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not the sample itself but the size of the electrochemical cell was reduced. Fig. 3 shows

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the electrochemical setup and the microcell used to measure local potentiodynamic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polarisation curves. The microcell consists of a glass capillary, ground at the tip and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: filled with the electrolyte (3 M HCl or 1 M HCl + 4 M NaCl). The tip diameter of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the capillary can be varied between 2 and 1000 μm. A layer of silicone rubber

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (specific resistivity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ω/cm) is applied at the tip to provide a seal. The counter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrode consists of a 0.5 mm thick platinum wire and a calomel-electrode serving as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reference electrode. It is connected to the glass capillary by an electrolyte bridge [18].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: switching to the microcell. After each experiment the sample is lowered and moved in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: x-y direction. It is adjusted to a new location after the glass capillary has been rinsed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The currents in electrochemical experiments at this micrometer scale are no longer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , typical for macroelectrochemical' polar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: isation experiments, but rather in the range of pA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and fA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . To detect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such extremely weak currents, several precautions are necessary:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Good shielding: To suppress electromagnetic interferences, the equipment is set up

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within a Faraday cage made of 3 mm thick copper plate. Due to the consistent use of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specially shielded wires and by keeping them as short as possible, electromagnetic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interference could be reduced to a minimum. During the testing all electrical wires

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were stored about 3 m away from the experiment.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: High resolution potentiostat: A modified, battery operated Jaissle potentiostat

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (type 1002T-NC-3) was used. The modification of the original apparatus (1002T-NC)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improved the current detection limit from 50 pA down to 50 fA. It consists of a spe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cial parallel operation amplifier which is also used for measuring electrochemical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: noise. Thus the detection limit is improved by a factor of 1000. In combination with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: double impedance converter (Jaissle Typ 1003) an input resistance of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input current of 20 fA was achieved. A low noise signal generator (Prodis Typ 1/16-1)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was used as input signal for the potentiostat.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Reduction of signal noise: The remaining noise (mostly 50 Hz) of the measured

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: signal (direct voltage signal which is proportional to the flowing current) has to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: further reduced: In the smallest range the output signal of the potentiostat is 1 V for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: R.A. Perren et al. / Corrosion Science 43 (2001) 707–726

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 10 nA. Thus fA currents result in μV signals. For good treatment of the direct

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: voltage a lock-in technique is applied. This technique allows the filtering and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amplifying of alternating voltages of certain frequencies out of a noisy signal. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: noisy signal has to be modified to a AC-signal by a selfmade chopper. The chopper

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frequency (2033 Hz) is fed to the lock-in amplifier (EG&G 5210) as a reference

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: signal. The output signal of the lock-in amplifier is a direct voltage, averaged over a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: certain time. With a time constant of 30 ms this setup corresponds to a 10-Hz filter.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.9. Choice of the electrolyte

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In potentiodynamic polarisation experiments the size of the exposed area affects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the results of the measured corrosion behaviour. Electrochemical measurements of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: small sample areas exhibit a better corrosion resistance than big scale measurements.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Suter et al. [19,20] showed that for areas below 500 μm in diameter the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential of an alloy increases with decreasing diameter of the microcapillary. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: probability of including weak spots in the material is diminished by smaller exposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: areas. The single phases of SDSS are in the range of 10–40 μm and the need for a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: very aggressive electrolyte becomes evident.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The most significant measure for the corrosion resistance is the pitting potential.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, the very high resistance against pitting of SDSS in combination with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: small size of the exposed single phases makes the microelectrochemical measure-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments of pitting potentials in SDSS at room temperature impossible. On the other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hand, chloride ion concentrations close to the solubility limit would plug the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: microcapillary tip. Therefore, an acid electrolyte was chosen, and the criteria for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance were the critical current density, the passivation potential and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the passive current density. Because of the ease of the handling of chloric acid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compared to sulfuric acid, the two electrolytes 3 M HCl and 1 M HCl + 4 M NaCl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were chosen for these small scale experiments. Measurements with 1 M HCl reveal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: very often three zero intersections and complicate the interpretation of the exper-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: iments. A stronger acid (3 M HCl) enlarges the active area of the anodic part reaction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and provides only one intersection point with the cathodic curve (part reaction).

layout_dets.text: 4. Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The macroelectrochemical measurements do not provide a clear ranking of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duplex alloys with respect to the corrosion resistance, although alloy 4 with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lowest PREN for a single phase and for the bulk alloy exhibits always the worst

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion behaviour. If only the weakest phase, i.e. the lowest PREN of a single

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phase, is responsible for the corrosion resistance, alloys 3 and 5 should reveal the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same corrosion behaviour. This is found for the corrosion experiments in neutral,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride ion containing environments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and LiCl concentration for pitting). In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentiodynamic experiments in chloric acid, however, alloy 5 with the higher ni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trogen content than alloy 3 has a better corrosion resistance (passivation potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and passive current density). In this case, the austenitic phase seems to be somewhat

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more susceptible to corrosion, if the ferrite posesses a similar corrosion resistance in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: PREN-units as the austenite. A slightly higher PREN of the austenite than of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: R.A. Perren et al. / Corrosion Science 43 (2001) 707–726

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferrite is beneficial with respect to corrosion and can be achieved by increasing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen content.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the macroelectrochemical polarisation experiments, the polarisation curves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: look as if the specimens consisted only of one phase and do not reveal the distinct

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contributions from the austenite and the ferrite phase in the active range. In this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context the small average phase size of the examined SDSS of 20 μm must be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentioned.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The microelectrochemical investigations in the region of the phase boundary,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where both the ferrite and the austenite are in the measured area, exhibit clearly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different contributions from the individual phases. The interaction of the single

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neighbour phases in these boundary measurement leads either to a kind of a su-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: perposition of the polarisation curves of the single phases or results in a separation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the two active ranges connected with a shift of the potentials.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The pitting resistance equivalent number, which is only a very rough empirical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach, does not take inhomogenities and precipitates into account. The micro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrochemical measurements, however, show, that the PREN are quite reliable to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assess the corrosion resistance of the individual phases of a SDSS. Moreover, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differences in the corrosion behaviour of both, the single phases of one alloy (due to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the partitioning), as well as for different alloys due to their different chemical com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: position can be detected.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. The corrosion resistance is determined by the weaker phase in neutral, chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing environments where pitting is the prevalent type of corrosion attack.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In strong acids where general corrosion is predominant, the austenitic phase

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seems to be more susceptible to corrosion (with similar PREN).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. While the microelectrochemical investigations reveal two different types of inter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: actions of the two phases in measurements of the boundary region, there is no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evidence of the two phase microstructure in the macroelectrochemical polarisa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion experiments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. The microelectrochemical measurements show a good correlation between the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: PREN of the single phases and the experimentally measured corrosion behaviour.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. The microelectrochemical method is an appropriate tool to determine the corro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion resistance of single phases in the range of 10 μm diameter.
